help.title: Help
help.sets: Sets contain either 20 standard amino acids or all 22, including selenocysteine (Sec, U) and pyrrolysine (Pyl, O).
help.classification1: By side-chain properties: nonpolar (G, A, V, L, I, M, P, F, W), polar uncharged (S, T, C, Y, N, Q), acidic (D, E), and basic (K, R, H). Aromatic ring: F, W, Y, H. Traditional teaching groups often list only F, W, and Y as aromatic. Hydrophobic aliphatic: A, V, L, I, M. Gly and Pro are singled out for their structural features.
help.classification2: Classifications vary among textbooks, especially for C, Y, and W. Histidine is basic, although its side chain is mostly neutral near pH 7. The quiz does not ask about a standard group or dietary essentiality for Sec and Pyl.
help.history: Name origins and discovery stories are included for all 22 amino acids. Practice works in both directions: amino acid to fact and fact to amino acid. Sources appear on cards and after answers.
help.stored: Progress is stored in this browser.
help.sourceCells: NCBI · The Molecular Composition of Cells
help.structures: Images show neutral free amino acids as skeletal formulas, formulas with explicit carbons and ball-and-stick 3D models. L configuration is preserved; glycine is achiral. Views and drawing styles change, but atoms and connectivity do not. A 3D model shows one possible molecular conformation.
